VANCOUVER (CP) — Former premier W. A. C. Bennett said Wednesday he expects to take his seat as opposition leader at the special session of

the Legislature Oct. 17.

In a brief telephone interview, Bennett was asked if he would be opposition leader at the special

session.

“T expect to,” he replied.

Bennett, who returned to Vancouver Tuesday ‘night after a holiday in Europe, said he plans to leave Vancouver today for his home in Kelowna. He said he would be, in Victoria this weekénd.

Former rehabilitation minister Phil Gaglardi said Bennett’s decision Wednesday to sit as leader of the opposition came as a pleasant surprise.

In a CBC radio interview in Vancouver Wed- nesday night, Gaglardi said his feeling was that Bennett will be extremely capable and effective as

opposition leader.

“I’m delighted,” said Gaglardi, “because no- body but nobody could be more effective at this

time.”

Industry Getting Off Lighter

Than Thought

Recreation and Conserva- tion Minister Robert Williams said Wednesday the gap be- tween the amount of bulk power used and the amount paid for by industry is even wider than he first thought

In his government policy statement Tuesday on B.C. Hydro, Williams had said

small power consumers were paying a disproportionately high rate in comparison to the low vate paid by industrial users.

He sought figures from the latest annual report of Hydro operations but the figures were not conclusive.

Wednesday in a forecast of power ‘use in the province in the 1972-73 fiscal year, the minister quoted figures from his department that predicted bulk industrial power users would consume 42 per cent of the power but would account for only 18.4 per cent of the revenue

The forecast said bulk in- dustrial users would need 7.7 billion kilowatt hours. For it they would pay slightly more than $42 million.
